title: "O, Not for These Alone I Pray,"
description: "O, Not for These Alone I Pray," in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emily Taylor wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 151, “"I Pray Not for These Alone."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "O, Not for these a-lone I pray," The dy-ing Sa-viour said; Though on his breast that mo-ment lay The loved dis-ci-ple's head;

lines: "O, Not for these alone I pray,"
Though on his breast that moment lay
Though to his eye that moment sprung
For those that eager round him hung,
His words of love to hear.
No, not for them alone he prayed; —
Whene'er their fervent prayer is made,
Sweet is the thought, when here we meet,
His feast of love to share;
And, 'mid the toils of life, how sweet

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Emily Taylor died in 1872.
credits: Words by Emily Taylor (1795–1872), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
